lines.spoken: Seven in ten online carts never check out. Cheapest Yes uses PayPal and AI to win them back, cheaply.
lines.written: Seven in ten online carts never check out. Cheapest Yes uses PayPal and AI to win them back, cheaply.

lines.spoken: Most stores answer with a blanket discount. That hands margin to shoppers who would have paid full price anyway.
lines.written: Most stores answer with a blanket discount. That hands margin to shoppers who would have paid full price anyway.

lines.spoken: Price isn't the only lever. On a two-forty cart, PayPal Pay Later costs about three sixty extra, and only when it's used. Ten percent off costs twenty-four.
lines.written: Price isn't the only lever. On a $240 cart, PayPal Pay Later costs about $3.60 extra, and only when it's used. 10% off costs $24.

lines.spoken: AI models score each shopper's session. A profit engine picks one incentive, or none. PayPal runs the checkout.
lines.written: AI models score each shopper's session. A profit engine picks one incentive, or none. PayPal runs the checkout.

lines.spoken: This shopper stalls at a two eighty eight total. The engine picks Pay Later, lifting the chance of a purchase from twenty to seventy three percent, and shows its reasons.
lines.written: This shopper stalls at a $288 total. The engine picks Pay Later, lifting the chance of a purchase from 20 to 73 percent, and shows its reasons.

lines.spoken: Then a real PayPal sandbox payment, using a test card. No real money moves.
lines.written: Then a real PayPal sandbox payment, using a test card. No real money moves.

lines.spoken: The capture and PayPal's fee are logged with the decision.
lines.written: The capture and PayPal's fee are logged with the decision.

lines.spoken: A loyal customer, already eighty percent likely to buy. The engine offers nothing, and keeps the margin.
lines.written: A loyal customer, already 80 percent likely to buy. The engine offers nothing, and keeps the margin.

lines.spoken: A student comparing prices in other tabs. Pay Later barely moves them, so here the cheapest yes is ten percent off.
lines.written: A student comparing prices in other tabs. Pay Later barely moves them, so here the cheapest yes is 10% off.

lines.spoken: Every option is scored on expected profit after fees. Prices never go above list, and budgets and per-shopper caps keep it honest.
lines.written: Every option is scored on expected profit after fees. Prices never go above list, and budgets and per-shopper caps keep it honest.

lines.spoken: On twenty thousand simulated shoppers, it beats a blanket discount by about eighty-three hundred dollars per thousand shoppers.
lines.written: On 20,000 simulated shoppers, it beats a blanket discount by about $8,300 per thousand shoppers.

lines.spoken: Every decision lands in an AG Grid log with its PayPal IDs, and a Gemini copilot answers the merchant's questions from that log.
lines.written: Every decision lands in an AG Grid log with its PayPal IDs, and a Gemini copilot answers the merchant's questions from that log.

lines.spoken: Honestly, always showing Pay Later gets most of the way, and without Pay Later, profit drops sixty-six hundred dollars per thousand shoppers. These are simulator results, not field results.
lines.written: Honestly, always showing Pay Later gets most of the way, and without Pay Later, profit drops $6,600 per thousand shoppers. These are simulator results, not field results.

lines.spoken: List price is the ceiling. Profit is the goal. PayPal Pay Later is the cheapest yes.
lines.written: List price is the ceiling. Profit is the goal. PayPal Pay Later is the cheapest yes.
